title: The History of Nintendo | From Playing Cards To Switch 2 | Gaming History
description: The history of Nintendo: founded in 1889 to make hanafuda cards, then Donkey Kong, the Famicom, Game Boy, Wii, Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 in 2025.

sections.heading: A company older than video games
sections.script: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are exploring the history of Nintendo, one of the oldest and most famous names in gaming. Mario, Zelda, Pokemon, Donkey Kong, Kirby and many more characters come from this company. But Nintendo is much older than any video game. It started more than a hundred years before the first Mario game, in a small workshop in Kyoto, Japan. In this video we will follow the whole story, from handmade playing cards to toys, arcade machines, home consoles, handhelds and the Nintendo Switch two. It is a story full of risky decisions and surprising turns. Let us begin in eighteen eighty nine.

sections.heading: Hanafuda cards in Kyoto
sections.script: Nintendo was founded on September twenty third, eighteen eighty nine, by Fusajiro Yamauchi in Kyoto. The company made hanafuda, traditional Japanese playing cards, and sold them by hand. In nineteen oh two, according to Nintendo's own timeline, it started producing western style playing cards in Japan too. Later, in nineteen fifty three, it became the first Japanese company to mass produce plastic playing cards. The business grew slowly but steadily, and in nineteen sixty three it took the name Nintendo Co., Ltd. At that point, nobody could imagine video games. Still, the habit of making fun things for families, and of experimenting with new materials, was already part of the company's culture.

sections.heading: Toys and the first electronics
sections.script: Hiroshi Yamauchi led the company from nineteen fifty until two thousand two, and he wanted Nintendo to try new things. In the nineteen sixties it moved into toys and other products. In nineteen sixty five, Gunpei Yokoi was hired to maintain the card-making machines, and he later became a famous inventor. In nineteen seventy Nintendo released the Beam Gun, described as Japan's first electronic toy, and it sold over a million units. Not every experiment worked, but the company learned how to build electronic products. In nineteen seventy seven it launched its first home video game machines, the Color TV-Game series, and that same year a young designer named Shigeru Miyamoto joined the company.

sections.heading: Game and Watch and Donkey Kong
sections.script: In nineteen eighty, Gunpei Yokoi created Game and Watch, a small handheld with one game and a clock. It sold more than forty million units in total, according to Wikipedia, and showed that people liked playing on the go. In nineteen eighty one came the arcade game Donkey Kong, designed under Shigeru Miyamoto. Its hero, first called Jumpman, later became Mario. Donkey Kong was a major hit and helped Nintendo grow in America, where the company had opened a subsidiary in New York City in nineteen seventy nine. This was the moment Nintendo stopped being a toy company with a few experiments and became a real video game company with characters people loved.

sections.heading: Famicom and the NES
sections.script: In July nineteen eighty three, Nintendo released the Family Computer, called the Famicom, in Japan. In nineteen eighty five, the Nintendo Entertainment System launched in North America together with Super Mario Bros. The game became a worldwide hit and defined what a platformer could be. Famicom and NES sales together reached roughly sixty two million units. The NES also helped rebuild interest in home consoles at a time when many people thought video games were a passing trend. Nintendo's strict approach to quality, and its ability to make characters that everyone recognized, built a model that the company still follows. The Legend of Zelda and Metroid soon joined Mario as pillars of the brand.

sections.heading: Game Boy and Super Nintendo
sections.script: In nineteen eighty nine, Nintendo launched the Game Boy, its first true handheld console with swappable games. It was not the most powerful handheld, but it was affordable and had a long battery life. The Game Boy and Game Boy Color together sold over one hundred eighteen million units, according to Wikipedia. In nineteen ninety the Super Famicom launched in Japan, and the Super Nintendo reached North America in nineteen ninety one. It brought classics such as Super Mario World and Zelda: A Link to the Past. Meanwhile, Pokemon Red and Blue arrived on Game Boy and sold over thirty one million copies, starting a franchise that would grow bigger than almost anyone expected.

sections.heading: Nintendo 64 and GameCube
sections.script: In nineteen ninety six, the Nintendo 64 launched in Japan in June and in the United States in September. It moved Mario and Zelda into full three dimensional worlds, and it sold about thirty three million units. Nintendo followed with the Game Boy Advance and the GameCube in two thousand one. The GameCube sold around twenty one point seven million units, fewer than rivals, but it is remembered for creative games and for its unusual controller. During this period the company faced tough competition, and the games business changed quickly. Nintendo kept to its own path, focusing on fun ideas instead of raw power, and that approach would soon lead to one of its biggest surprises.

sections.heading: DS, Wii and a new audience
sections.script: In two thousand two, Satoru Iwata became president of Nintendo, ending the Yamauchi family line at the top of the company. Under his leadership Nintendo launched the Nintendo DS in two thousand four, with its two screens and touch controls, and the Wii in two thousand six, with motion controls that invited whole families to play. These products reached people who had never owned a console before. Iwata led the company until two thousand fifteen. After him, Shuntaro Furukawa became president, according to Wikipedia. Later machines included the three D S in two thousand eleven and the Wii U in two thousand twelve. Not every device was a giant success, but Nintendo kept experimenting.

sections.heading: Nintendo Switch changes everything
sections.script: In two thousand seventeen, Nintendo launched the Switch, a console that works both at home on a TV and as a handheld. Games like Breath of the Wild, Super Mario Odyssey and Animal Crossing helped it become a huge success. Reports show the Switch family passed one hundred fifty million units, and later results put it above one hundred fifty three million. Nintendo also expanded beyond games, with the first Nintendo TOKYO store opening in twenty nineteen, Super Nintendo World at Universal Studios Japan in twenty twenty one and The Super Mario Bros. Movie in twenty twenty three. The Switch showed that a simple idea, played well, can be more powerful than the latest hardware.
images: wiki:The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

sections.heading: Why Nintendo keeps its own path
sections.script: One thing connects every era of Nintendo, from hanafuda cards to the Switch. The company likes to ask how people can have fun in a new way, rather than only asking how powerful a machine can be. Motion controls on the Wii, two screens on the DS and the hybrid design of the Switch all came from that attitude. Its characters, such as Mario, Link and the Pokemon, are loved by families all over the world. Wikipedia reports that Nintendo consoles have sold over eight hundred seventy million units in total, with more than six billion games sold. That is the result of more than a century of patient experimenting.

sections.heading: Switch 2 and your favorite Nintendo moment
sections.script: On June fifth, twenty twenty five, Nintendo launched the Nintendo Switch two. Reports said it sold almost ten point four million units in its first one hundred eighteen days, making it the company's fastest-selling system, with Mario Kart World as a launch game. From a hanafuda workshop in Kyoto to a global entertainment brand, Nintendo's story is more than one hundred thirty years long. So here is our question for you. What is your favorite Nintendo console or game of all time? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to the channel for more gaming history. Thanks for watching, and we will see you in the next video.

joke: Nintendo started with playing cards, so technically Mario was always going to be dealt a good hand.
